హియర్ ఈజ్ ది కంప్లీట్ లైన్-బై-లైన్ తెలుగు అనువాదం మరియు భావం (Complete line-by-line Telugu meaning of the song):
పల్లవి (Chorus)
Jab zid pe aa gayi Parvati / Samjhaane pahunche Saptarishi
భావం: పార్వతీ దేవి శివుడిని మాత్రమే వివాహం చేసుకోవాలని మొండిగా పట్టుబట్టినప్పుడు, ఆమెకు నచ్చజెప్పడానికి సప్తరుషులు (ఏడుగురు గొప్ప మునులు) వచ్చారు.
Kaay zid kar rai / Kaay ko mar rai / Aise var ke laane
భావం: "అమ్మా! ఎందుకు ఇలాంటి మొండి పట్టు పడుతున్నావు? ఇలాంటి వరుడి కోసం ఎందుకు నీ ప్రాణాలను (తపస్సుతో) కష్టపెట్టుకుంటున్నావు?" అని మునులు అడిగారు.
Jaake sees pe Ganga / Aur gale mein daare phir rahe saanp
భావం: "ఎవరి తలపై గంగానది ఉందో, మెడలో పాములను వేసుకుని తిరుగుతుంటాడో.. అలాంటి వాడా నీకు మొగుడు?"
Itne seedhe-saade hain, / Sab kehte Bholenath… Bholenath
భావం: ఆయన ఎంత అమాయకుడు మరియు నిరాడంబరుడు అంటే, అందుకే అందరూ ఆయన్ను 'భోలేనాథ్' అని పిలుస్తారు.

చరణం 1 (Stanza 1)
Na khapra na chhapra / Na phoos ki dhare madaiya
భావం: ఆయనకు ఒక పెంకుటిల్లు లేదు, పైకప్పు లేదు, కనీసం గడ్డితో వేసిన చిన్న గుడిసె కూడా లేదు (ఆయనకు ఇల్లే లేదు, శ్మశానంలో ఉంటాడు).
Ka khaave ko dharo wahaan / Bas rovat rahat ladaiyaa
భావం: అక్కడ తినడానికి ఏముంది? చుట్టూ కేవలం భూతప్రేతాలు, గొడవలు, ఏడుపులే ఉంటాయి.
Bhesh dhare avadhoot phire, / Ab tumse ka kahe
భావం: ఒక అవధూత (దిగంబర/పిచ్చివాడి) లాంటి వేషం వేసుకుని తిరుగుతుంటాడు, ఆయన గురించి నీకు ఇంకా ఏం చెప్పాలి?
Binnu Dora daangar le ghoomein / Ve inke kachhue naiyya
భావం: ఎటువంటి ఆస్తిపాస్తులు, కనీసం కట్టే తాడు కూడా లేకుండా కేవలం ఒక ముసలి ఎద్దును (నందిని) వేసుకుని తిరుగుతాడు. ఆయన దగ్గర ఏమీ లేదు.

చరణం 2 (Stanza 2)
Jataa lataa na kabahu sanwaare / Deesat maha bhayankar
భావం: ఆయన తన జడలను ఎప్పుడూ సరిచేసుకోడు, చూడటానికి చాలా భయంకరంగా ఉంటాడు.
Moodh pe aadho chanda / Aur belaa pe ghoome Shankar
భావం: తలపై సగం చంద్రుడిని ధరించి, ఎద్దుపై ఎక్కి ఊరంతా తిరుగుతుంటాడు ఈ శంకరుడు.
Ram naam ke rasiya hain ve / Aur unhein kya chaahne
భావం: ఆయన ఎప్పుడూ 'రామ నామ' జపంలోనే మునిగి తేలుతుంటాడు, ఆయనకు సంసారంపై గానీ, లోకంపై గానీ ఎలాంటి ఆశలు లేవు.
Kaamdev ke mardanhaari / Ghar-grihasthi kya jaane / Are ghar-grihasthi kya jaane
భావం: మన్మథుడినే భస్మం చేసిన జితేంద్రియుడు ఆయన. అలాంటి వ్యక్తికి ఇల్లు, వాకిలి, సంసారం మరియు గృహస్థాశ్రమం గురించి ఏం తెలుస్తుంది? అసలు సంసార సుఖాలు ఆయనకేం తెలుసు?

ముగింపు (Outro)
Kaay zid kar rai / Kaay tap kar rai / Aise bar ke laane...
భావం: కాబట్టి అమ్మా పార్వతీ! ఇలాంటి వరుడి కోసం ఎందుకు అంత కఠినమైన తపస్సు చేస్తున్నావు? నీ పట్టు విడనాడమని సప్తరుషులు పార్వతీ దేవిని వేడుకుంటారు. (కానీ పార్వతీ దేవి తన పట్టు వదలకుండా శివుడినే వివాహం చేసుకుంటుంది).

1. माता सती और भगवान शिव का विवाह!

भगवान शिव की पहली पत्नी का नाम माता सती था। वे राजा दक्ष की पुत्री थीं।
माता सती ने भगवान शिव से विवाह किया था, लेकिन उनके पिता दक्ष भगवान शिव को पसंद नहीं करते थे।
एक बार राजा दक्ष ने एक बड़ा यज्ञ आयोजित किया। उन्होंने भगवान शिव और माता सती को आमंत्रित नहीं किया। इसके बावजूद माता सती वहाँ पहुँचीं। वहाँ अपने पिता द्वारा भगवान शिव के प्रति अपमानजनक व्यवहार देखकर उन्हें बहुत दुख हुआ।

कथा के अनुसार, माता सती ने यज्ञ में अपने प्राण त्याग दिए। यह जानकर भगवान शिव अत्यंत दुखी हुए। आगे की कथा में शिव के क्रोध, दक्ष के यज्ञ के विनाश और बाद में दक्ष को जीवन मिलने का वर्णन आता है।
इसके बाद माता सती ने अगले जन्म में हिमालय के राजा हिमवान और रानी मैना के घर पार्वती के रूप में जन्म लिया

2.  माता पार्वती ने भगवान शिव को ही पति क्यों चुना?

माता पार्वती बचपन से ही भगवान शिव के प्रति विशेष श्रद्धा रखती थीं। कथा के अनुसार, देवर्षि नारद ने उनके माता-पिता को बताया कि पार्वती का विवाह भगवान शिव से हो सकता है।

पार्वती के माता-पिता हिमवान और मैना थे। वे अपनी बेटी का विवाह अच्छे वर से करना चाहते थे। पार्वती ने मन में भगवान शिव को अपना पति मान लिया।
लेकिन शिव साधारण राजकुमार की तरह नहीं रहते थे। वे हिमालय में ध्यान करते, सांसारिक सुख-सुविधाओं से दूर रहते और साधु जैसा जीवन बिताते थे।
पार्वती के लिए यह केवल बाहरी रूप का मामला नहीं था। वे शिव को ही अपना जीवनसाथी बनाना चाहती थीं।

3. माता पार्वती की कठोर तपस्या......

पार्वती ने अपने राजमहल के सुख छोड़कर हिमालय में तपस्या शुरू कर दी।

कथा में बताया जाता है कि उन्होंने शुरुआत में फल खाए, फिर गिरे हुए पत्ते खाए और अंत में पत्ते खाना भी छोड़ दिया। उनकी इस तपस्या के कारण उन्हें अपर्णा नाम से भी जाना गया।

उनके माता-पिता उन्हें समझाते थे कि वे इतनी कठिन तपस्या न करें, लेकिन पार्वती अपने संकल्प पर दृढ़ रहीं। वे भगवान शिव को ही अपना पति बनाना चाहती थीं। 
यहाँ तपस्या का अर्थ है अपने लक्ष्य के लिए कठिन साधना करना।

कथा के अनुसार, सात महान ऋषियों को पार्वती के पास भेजा गया। उन्हें सप्तऋषि कहा जाता है।
उन्होंने पार्वती से कहा कि वे जिस शिव को अपना पति बनाना चाहती हैं, उनका रहन-सहन दूसरे राजकुमारों जैसा नहीं है।

उन्होंने शिव के बारे में इन बातों का उल्लेख किया:

वे सिर पर जटाएँ रखते हैं, जिनमें गंगा विराजमान हैं।

उनके गले में साँप रहता है।
वे शरीर पर भस्म लगाते हैं।
वे राजमहल में रहने के बजाय जंगलों और श्मशान जैसे स्थानों में रहते हैं।
वे सांसारिक सुख-सुविधाओं से दूर रहते हैं।
ऋषियों का आशय था कि पार्वती को अपने विवाह के निर्णय पर दोबारा विचार करना चाहिए।

काहे ज़िद कर रही, काहे को मर रही, ऐसे वर के लाने…”

इसका अर्थ है: तुम ऐसे वर को पाने के लिए इतनी ज़िद क्यों कर रही हो और इतनी कठिन तपस्या क्यों कर रही हो, जिसके सिर पर गंगा और गले में साँप हैं

सप्तऋषियों के बाद कथा के एक प्रसिद्ध रूप में भगवान शिव स्वयं एक युवा ब्राह्मण का रूप धारण करके पार्वती के पास पहुँचे।

उन्होंने माता पार्वती से पूछा कि वे शिव को ही पति क्यों बनाना चाहती हैं। उन्होंने शिव के रूप और जीवनशैली की आलोचना भी की।

माता पार्वती यह सुनकर नाराज़ हो गईं। उन्होंने कहा कि शिव को समझे बिना उनके बारे में ऐसी बातें नहीं कहनी चाहिए। उन्होंने स्पष्ट कर दिया कि वे किसी दूसरे को अपना पति नहीं चुनेंगी।

text:
“Parvati” — English Meaning
Shambhu, Shiv Shambhu! Bholenath!
O Shambhu, O Lord Shiva! O innocent/simple-hearted Lord!
Jab zid pe aa gayi Parvati…
When Parvati became determined and refused to give up,
the Saptarishis (seven great sages) came to convince her.
Kaay zid kar rahi, kaay ko mar rahi,
aise var ke laane…
“Why are you being so stubborn?
Why are you putting yourself through such hardship?
Why do you want to marry such a man?”
Jaake sees pe Ganga aur gale mein daale phir rahe saanp,
itne seedhe-saade hain sab kehte Bholenath…
“He has the Ganga flowing from his head,
and snakes around his neck!
And yet everyone calls him innocent and simple—Bholenath!”
Na khapra na chhapra,
na foos ki dhare madaiya…
“He doesn't even have a proper roof over his head,
not a tiled house, not even a thatched hut.”
Ka khaave ko dharo wahan,
bas rovat rahat ladaiyaan…
“What would you even eat there?
There would be nothing but hardship and struggle.”
Bhesh dhare avdhoot phire,
ab tumse ka-kahe Binnu…
“He wanders around dressed like an ascetic,
what more can we possibly tell you?”
Dora daangar le ghoomein,
ve inke kachhuye naiyaan…
“He wanders around with his belongings/animals,
he doesn't even have the comforts of an ordinary household.”
Then the sages again ask:
“Why are you so stubborn?
Why are you performing such severe penance?
Why do you want to bring this man as your husband?”
But Parvati remains determined.
The next verse
Jata lata na kabahun sanvaare,
deesat maha bhayankar…
“He never even takes care of or styles his matted hair,
and he looks absolutely terrifying.”
Moor pe aadho chanda aur,
bela pe ghoome Shankar…
“He has a crescent moon upon his head,
and Shankar wanders about in his own divine way.”
Ram naam ke rasiya hain ve,
aur unhein kya chaahne…
“He is immersed in the love of Lord Rama's name.
What else could someone like him possibly desire?”
Kaamdev ke mardanhaari,
ghar-grihasthi kya jaane…
“He is the one who defeated Kamadeva,
so what would he know about ordinary married household life?”
Again the sages try to convince Parvati, but she refuses to change her mind.
Bhole Bam Bhole…
Jai Jai Shiv Shambhu!
Praise to innocent Bholenath!
Victory to Lord Shiva!
🌸 Overall meaning
The song is basically a playful conversation between the Saptarishis and Parvati. The sages are trying to tell Parvati:
“Why do you want Shiva? He looks frightening, has snakes around his neck, lives like an ascetic, has no conventional home or possessions, and has nothing to do with ordinary worldly life.”
But Parvati's determination doesn't change. She wants Shiva despite all these unconventional qualities.
So underneath the humorous lyrics, the song shows Parvati's unwavering devotion and determination toward Shiva—she sees beyond his appearance and unconventional lifestyle.

The underlying joke

The Saptaṛṣis are deliberately describing Shiva from the perspective of an ordinary worldly family trying to find a suitable husband for their daughter:

He has snakes instead of ornaments.
He has Ganga in his hair instead of a conventional royal appearance.
He has matted hair and a terrifying appearance.
He has no house, wealth, cattle or worldly possessions.
He dresses like a wandering ascetic.
He has destroyed Kamadeva, so he supposedly knows nothing about romance.
And, most importantly, he has no idea how to run a household.

The humor is that the sages are trying to portray Mahadev's very divine qualities as terrible qualifications for a husband. Parvati, of course, sees exactly what they fail to see: the ascetic Shiva is the supreme Lord she has chosen through her tapasya.

text:
Shambhu, Shiv Shambhu! Bholenath!
O Shambhu, O Lord Shiva! O innocent/simple-hearted Lord!
Jab zid pe aa gayi Parvati…
When Parvati became determined and refused to give up,
the Saptarishis (seven great sages) came to convince her.
Kaay zid kar rahi, kaay ko mar rahi,
aise var ke laane…
“Why are you being so stubborn?
Why are you putting yourself through such hardship?
Why do you want to marry such a man?”
Jaake sees pe Ganga aur gale mein daale phir rahe saanp,
itne seedhe-saade hain sab kehte Bholenath…
“He has the Ganga flowing from his head,
and snakes around his neck!
And yet everyone calls him innocent and simple—Bholenath!”
Na khapra na chhapra,
na foos ki dhare madaiya…
“He doesn't even have a proper roof over his head,
not a tiled house, not even a thatched hut.”
Ka khaave ko dharo wahan,
bas rovat rahat ladaiyaan…
“What would you even eat there?
There would be nothing but hardship and struggle.”
Bhesh dhare avdhoot phire,
ab tumse ka-kahe Binnu…
“He wanders around dressed like an ascetic,
what more can we possibly tell you?”
Dora daangar le ghoomein,
ve inke kachhuye naiyaan…
“He wanders around with his belongings/animals,
he doesn't even have the comforts of an ordinary household.”
Then the sages again ask:
“Why are you so stubborn?
Why are you performing such severe penance?
Why do you want to bring this man as your husband?”
But Parvati remains determined.
The next verse
Jata lata na kabahun sanvaare,
deesat maha bhayankar…
“He never even takes care of or styles his matted hair,
and he looks absolutely terrifying.”
Moor pe aadho chanda aur,
bela pe ghoome Shankar…
“He has a crescent moon upon his head,
and Shankar wanders about in his own divine way.”
Ram naam ke rasiya hain ve,
aur unhein kya chaahne…
“He is immersed in the love of Lord Rama's name.
What else could someone like him possibly desire?”
Kaamdev ke mardanhaari,
ghar-grihasthi kya jaane…
“He is the one who defeated Kamadeva,
so what would he know about ordinary married household life?”
Again the sages try to convince Parvati, but she refuses to change her mind.
Bhole Bam Bhole…
Jai Jai Shiv Shambhu!
Praise to innocent Bholenath!
Victory to Lord Shiva!
🌸 Overall meaning
The song is basically a playful conversation between the Saptarishis and Parvati. The sages are trying to tell Parvati:
“Why do you want Shiva? He looks frightening, has snakes around his neck, lives like an ascetic, has no conventional home or possessions, and has nothing to do with ordinary worldly life.”
But Parvati's determination doesn't change. She wants Shiva despite all these unconventional qualities.
So underneath the humorous lyrics, the song shows Parvati's unwavering devotion and determination toward Shiva—she sees beyond his appearance and unconventional lifestyle.
